scenarios.desc: Self-check of a PR description draft names the helper scripts
scenarios.input: I wrote a PR description in draft.md. Before I post it, run a prose self-check on it. Which scripts do you run first, and what exit code means the lint pass is clean? Answer in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: SKILL.md Process: run prose_lint.py (Layers 1 and 2, exits 1 on any high-severity finding) and burstiness.py over the artifact, then do Layer 4 by hand. A generic answer would proofread by eye.

scenarios.desc: Does a draft read as AI-written, with structural tells present
scenarios.input: Does this read as AI-written? "Honestly, this change is not just a refactor, it's a rethink of the loader. Want me to also update the docs?" Name the specific tells and how you would fix each. Answer in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: SKILL.md Layer 2 lists contrast_framing, trailing_offer, and signposting as the three scripted structural tells, each with a prescribed fix (state the claim directly, delete the offer, delete the opener).

scenarios.desc: Lint exits 0 but the prose may still be empty
scenarios.input: prose_lint.py exited 0 on my retrospective, so I think it is done. Is that enough before I emit it? Answer in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: SKILL.md Anti-Patterns: stopping at exit 0 clears Layers 1 and 2 only. Layer 4 requires naming the one disagreeable claim per paragraph, otherwise the paragraph is filler.

scenarios.desc: Code style review, which belongs to style-enforcement (negative)
scenarios.input: Check my Python module for naming conventions, import order, and line length against the repo style guide. Answer in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: The description says 'Do NOT use for code style (use style-enforcement)'. This is a style request about code, not an AI-tell audit of prose.
